method: lsctl text injection into the dev build; DeepSeek judge

scenarios.name: Founder interview: intro, basics, flowchart, sequence diagram

checks.them: Let's do something visual. Can you draw a flowchart of how a chat message goes from the user tapping send to the streamed reply showing on screen in our app?

card.problem: Draw a flowchart of a chat message from tapping send to the streamed reply showing on screen
card.heard: draw a flowchart, tap send to streamed reply on screen
card.say: I'll draw the main path first. The user taps send, and the app saves the message locally and shows it right away. Then it sends the request to the backend, and the backend streams the reply back. The app reads each piece and updates the screen as it arrives.
card.type: draw@chat message flow: flowchart TD ⏎ A[User taps send] --> B[Save message locally] ⏎ B --> C[Show message on screen] ⏎ C --> D[Send request to backend] ⏎ D --> E[Backend streams reply] ⏎ E --> F[App reads each chunk] ⏎ F --> G[Update screen]
card.then: Next, I'd add what happens when the connection drops mid-stream.

checks.them: What happens in that flow if the network drops halfway through the reply? Add it to the diagram.

card.problem: Draw a flowchart of a chat message from tapping send to the streamed reply showing on screen
card.constraints: ["Network can drop halfway through the streamed reply"]
card.heard: network drops halfway through the reply, add it to the diagram
card.say: Okay, I'll add the drop path to the diagram. If the network drops, the app keeps the partial reply on screen and marks it as not finished. It saves the last chunk it got, then reconnects and asks for the rest from that point. The server would need to keep the reply and send only the missing part.
card.type: draw@chat-flow: flowchart TD ⏎ F[App reads each chunk] --> H[Network drops] ⏎ H --> I[Keep partial reply, mark unfinished] ⏎ I --> J[Reconnect from last chunk] ⏎ J --> E
card.then: Next, I'd cover what the user sees while it reconnects.

checks.them: Good. Now a different one: draw me a sequence diagram of login, including what happens when the access token expires and the app refreshes it.

card.problem: Draw a flowchart of a chat message from tapping send to the streamed reply showing on screen
card.constraints: ["Network can drop halfway through the streamed reply"]
card.heard: draw a sequence diagram of login with token refresh
card.say: Okay, I'll start a new diagram for login. The app sends the username and password to the backend. The backend checks them and returns an access token and a refresh token. The app saves both and opens the main screen. Later, when a request comes back as expired, the app sends the refresh token and gets a new access token, then repeats the failed request once.
card.type: draw@: sequenceDiagram ⏎ participant App ⏎ participant Server ⏎ App->>Server: Login with username and password ⏎ Server-->>App: Access token + refresh token ⏎ App->>Server: Request with access token ⏎ Server-->>App: 401 token expired ⏎ App->>Server: Refresh token ⏎ Server-->>App: New access token ⏎ App->>Server: Retry request with new token ⏎ Server-->>App: Data
card.then: Next, I'd cover what happens if the refresh token is also expired.
